title: Frontend: Sortable List
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Sortable List. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({items=[A,B,C]}). Render ordered li[data-id=LABEL], draggable with drag/drop reordering, and Move down buttons[data-down=LABEL]. Dropping one row on another inserts at the target original index. Move down swaps with the next row and clamps at the end. Output comma-joined order in [data-testid=order]. Labels are unique. Preserve immutable identity.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent order as IDs or immutable records and compute a new array for each move.
alternativeApproaches: Virtualize a large list while keeping keyboard announcements and drag hit targets consistent.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: First/last item; cancelled move; repeated reorder.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
